items.context: Round 1 selected option C: merge Prompts into Settings to keep 5 tabs. After exploring both pages, this is highly impractical. PromptsPage is ~600+ lines with a Monaco editor, resizable panels, version comparison, and simulation playground. SettingsPage is a simple form (~400 lines). They serve completely different domains (skill management vs user preferences). Merging would create a confusing 'god page' with unrelated tabs. The original concern was mobile navigation with 6 tabs.

options.label: Keep 6 tabs — use icon-only mobile nav
options.rationale: Cleanest separation. Dashboard gets its own tab. Use lucide icons with short labels on mobile bottom nav. Most dashboard apps handle 5-6 bottom tabs fine (e.g., GitHub mobile has 5).

options.label: Keep 6 tabs — use scrollable/overflow mobile nav
options.rationale: All tabs keep full labels. Horizontal scroll or 'More' menu on mobile. Slightly harder to discover hidden tabs.

options.label: Proceed with Prompts/Settings merge despite complexity
options.rationale: Honors round 1 decision. Would require significant refactoring of both pages into a tabbed container. High risk of UX regression.

items.topic: Dashboard component structure and data fetching pattern
items.context: The swarm-manager UI uses two patterns: (1) Zustand stores for pages with complex state (BacklogPage, ScenariosPage, ExecutionPage) and (2) useQuery for simpler pages (PromptsPage, SettingsPage). The Dashboard aggregates data from multiple domains but doesn't modify it — it's read-only.

options.label: useQuery composing existing service calls
options.rationale: Dashboard is read-only with no complex local state. Use useQuery with the overview endpoint + execution list for the activity feed. Simpler, no new store needed. React Query handles caching and refetch interval natively (refetchInterval: 60000 for polling).

options.label: New Zustand dashboard-store with periodic fetch
options.rationale: Centralized state with explicit fetch methods. Consistent with BacklogPage pattern. But adds a store for what's essentially cached server state — over-engineered for a read-only view.

items.topic: Widget layout approach for responsive design
items.context: The dashboard needs to display 4 widget areas (summary stats, blocked items, initiative progress, recent activity). Layout must work on both desktop (card grid) and mobile (stacked). The existing UI uses TailwindCSS with responsive breakpoints.

options.label: CSS Grid with responsive breakpoints
options.rationale: Use Tailwind grid classes: 2-column on desktop (stats + blocked on row 1, initiatives + activity on row 2), single column on mobile. Clean, minimal CSS. Consistent with how other pages use Tailwind.

options.label: Flexbox with wrap
options.rationale: More flexible sizing per widget. Widgets fill available space naturally. But harder to get consistent grid alignment.

items.context: The activity feed widget needs recent execution runs. The overview API doesn't include execution data — it only has backlog items, initiatives, and dependency graph. Execution data comes from a separate /execution endpoint. The question is whether to add execution data to the overview API or compose client-side.

options.label: Separate useQuery call to /execution endpoint
options.rationale: No backend changes needed (aligns with 'no new API endpoints' constraint). Fetch last N executions client-side with a limit param. Two parallel fetches on mount.

options.label: Extend overview API to include recent executions
options.rationale: Single endpoint, single fetch. But requires backend changes and expands acceptance_allow to include api/ files. Violates the 'no new backend endpoints' constraint from round 1.

items.context: The current plan has a generic testing section. For a UI-only page with no new backend work, tests should focus on component rendering and data integration. The codebase uses vitest + testing-library for component tests.

options.label: Component unit tests + route integration test
options.rationale: Unit tests for each widget (SummaryCards, BlockedItems, InitiativeProgress, RecentActivity) with mock data covering loading/error/populated states. One integration test verifying DashboardPage fetches and renders. Route test verifying / loads Dashboard.

options.label: Snapshot tests + minimal integration
options.rationale: Faster to write. Snapshot tests catch unintended UI changes. But brittle — snapshots break on any styling change and provide low signal.

items.text: The overview endpoint (/api/v1/overview) exists in the Go backend but is NOT yet registered in the UI's api-endpoints.ts. The plan will need to add an 'overview' entry to API_ENDPOINTS and create a minimal overview-service.ts (or add a method to an existing service). This is a small addition — just a new endpoint constant and a typed fetch wrapper.

The UI already has reusable components that map well to dashboard widgets: Card (with padding variants), StatusLegend (for status colors), ErrorState (for per-widget error handling), PageLoadingState, InlineLoadingIndicator, and ResponsiveList. Status color maps (BACKLOG_STATUS_COLORS, SCENARIO_STATUS_ICONS) are also available in types/constants.ts. No new shared primitives needed.

plan_updates: Round 2: Surfaced Prompts/Settings merge risk as a new decision. Added component architecture decisions (data fetching pattern, layout approach, activity feed source). Refined testing plan specificity. Updated technical context with discovery that overview endpoint is missing from UI api-endpoints.ts.
